title: Hooking Up Washing Machine Plumbing: Copper Pipe, Soldering, and Stainless Braided Hoses
summary: This This Old House episode demonstrates assembling a washing machine water-supply hookup by framing a small mounting box, securing copper supply runs with bell hangers, installing a dedicated shut-off valve, fluxing and soldering copper joints, branching a washer feed with a T-fitting, and finally replacing worn rubber hoses with stainless steel braided supply hoses, followed by restoring water and testing the system for laundry readiness.
topics: hot and cold water supply lines
cutting copper pipe and pipe cutting

sections.title: Box framing for plumbing install
concepts: frame with top and bottom plates
sections.description: Presenter constructs a small box frame to mount plumbing hardware before routing water supply lines.

sections.title: Mounting bell hangers and feeding copper
sections.description: Two marks are made to mount bell hangers; copper pipe is routed into the bell-shaped clips that hold the line.

sections.title: Preparing copper fittings for soldering
sections.description: Pipes and fittings are cleaned, fittings are brushed, flux is applied, preparing for soldering.

sections.title: Valve installation and branch planning
sections.description: A washing machine shut-off valve is prepared; plan to connect a T-fitting to branch the washer feed from the hot line.

sections.title: Soldering and retrofit assembly
sections.description: Flushed fittings are fluxed and soldered with attention to avoid excessive solder that could damage adjacent joints.

sections.title: Replacing hoses and re-securing supply lines
sections.description: Old rubber hoses are replaced with stainless steel braided supply hoses; fittings are seated into place.

sections.title: Testing water supply and final confirmation
sections.description: Cold and hot valves are opened to restore water; the system is confirmed ready for laundry use.

featured_techniques.technique: Install copper bell hangers to support piping
Branching supply with a T-fitting for washer line
Replace rubber hoses with stainless steel braided supply hoses
Test water supply by opening cold and hot valves
